notes: Stress variant: 5 rows, long labels, captions off, no intro (frame 1 is mid-roll on row 1). Maths: $10,000 × 22% = $2,200 (IRS flat withholding rate for supplemental wages up to $1M, Pub. 15); × 6.2% = $620 (Social Security, below the wage base); × 1.45% = $145 (Medicare); × 5% = $500 (assumed state rate); withheld $2,200 + $620 + $145 + $500 = $3,465; $10,000 − $3,465 = $6,535 = 65.35%; check $2,200 + $620 + $145 + $500 + $6,535 = $10,000. State range: 9 states have no wage income tax; California's top rate is 13.3%.
